\begin{abstract}
This report summarizes implementations and experiments for the CAe assignment in the Deep Learning and Neural Networks course. We cover Image Captioning (encoder-decoder with attention), CLIP-style contrastive learning, Urban Sound classification with Wav2Vec and CNN baselines, LoRA fine-tuning for sentiment analysis, and adversarial attack experiments (FGSM and PGD) with adversarial training. Reproducible code, scripts, and publication-quality figures are included in the project repository.
\end{abstract}

\begin{IEEEkeywords}
Image captioning, Attention, CLIP, Contrastive learning, Wav2Vec, LoRA, Adversarial attacks, FGSM, PGD
\end{IEEEkeywords}

\section{Introduction}
We tackle multiple tasks combining computer vision, natural language processing, self-supervised learning, and adversarial robustness. The repository includes modular code, notebooks, and assets suitable for inclusion in IEEE-format reports.

\section{Q1: Image Captioning}
\subsection{Dataset and preprocessing}
We used a Flickr/COCO subset (images + Persian captions) provided with the assignment. Preprocessing includes lowercasing, punctuation removal, emoji handling, vocabulary creation (including special tokens \texttt{<start>, <end>, <pad>, <unk>}), and a PyTorch DataLoader with a custom collate function that pads sequences to batch-max length.

\subsection{Model}
We implemented an encoder-decoder architecture. The encoder is a pretrained VGG16-based feature extractor (final classifier removed and frozen during training). The decoder is an LSTM with an additive attention mechanism similar to \cite{xu2015show}. Embedding size: 300, hidden size: 512.

\subsection{Training and evaluation}
Training uses Cross-Entropy Loss with teacher forcing; inference uses greedy decoding. We saved the best checkpoints and exported training loss curves and sample generated captions.

BLEU scores (BLEU-1 to BLEU-4) were computed using sacreBLEU \cite{post-2018-call}. The implementation and evaluation scripts are available in `codes/q1_image_captioning`.

\section{Q1.5: CLIP-style contrastive learning}
We implemented an image encoder based on ViT (timm model) and a small LSTM text encoder, projecting both modalities into a joint embedding space and training with an InfoNCE loss (temperature parameter learned). Figure~\ref{fig:clip_sim} shows a demo similarity heatmap.

\end{figure}

\section{Q2: Urban Sound Classification}
\subsection{Dataset and preprocessing}
We prepared UrbanSound8K metadata and generated mel-spectrograms for input to both CNN and Wav2Vec-based experiments. Short synthetic examples and saved spectrograms are included in the `q2_urban_sound/images` folder.

\subsection{Experiments}
We compare: (1) CNN trained from scratch on mel-spectrograms, and (2) Wav2Vec features (facebook/wav2vec2-base) in three regimes: frozen backbone, partial freeze, and full fine-tuning. Metrics: Accuracy, Macro F1, and confusion matrices.

\section{Q3: LoRA Fine-tuning for Sentiment Analysis}
We fine-tuned `meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B` with LoRA adapters on the `emotion` dataset from Hugging Face using stratified sampling (train=1500, val=50, test=100). We used rank $r=8$, alpha=32, and lora\_dropout=0.1 and employed mixed precision training.

\section{Q4: Adversarial Attacks and Defenses}
\subsection{Attack implementation}
We implemented FGSM and PGD attacks (code in `codes/q4_adversarial/attacks.py`). For PGD we tested both 5 and 10 iterations and varied $\epsilon$. See Figure~\ref{fig:adv_samples}.

\begin{figure}[t]
    \centering
    \includegraphics[width=0.48\textwidth]{fig-adversarial-samples-eps0.1.pdf}
    \caption{Original (top row) vs. FGSM perturbed samples (bottom row) from the adversarial demo.}
    \label{fig:adv_samples}
\end{figure}

\subsection{Adversarial training}
We implemented adversarial training by generating PGD adversarial examples during training. Performance vs. $\epsilon$ is plotted and compared to standard training.
